items.detail: Wall Street steadied Monday: the **S&P 500 closed essentially flat at 7,413.18** (+0.02%) and the **Dow rose 262.83 points (0.51%) to 52,210.08**, but the **Nasdaq slipped 0.18% to 24,932.08** as a fresh chip rout capped the tech-heavy index.
items.why: A deeper plunge in oil lifted the Dow and rate-sensitive names, but an intraday reversal in semiconductors dragged the Nasdaq back into the red.

items.detail: A new, sharper leg of the chip selloff hit Monday: **Nvidia fell ~5%**, **AMD dropped more than 8%**, **ASML lost over 7%** and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF slid ~4%, extending its one-month decline past 9%.
items.why: A report that a Chinese firm cracked a lithography manufacturing step Western chipmakers thought they still controlled sparked fears the AI hardware moat is narrowing, forcing leveraged sellers out of equipment and chip names.

items.detail: Crude accelerated its slide, with **Brent futures down 8.7% to $88.36** and **WTI off 7.5% to $82.61** — a second straight session of heavy losses that unwinds the entire Middle East war premium.
items.why: President Trump said the U.S. and Iran are in talks to end the conflict and strikes have paused, easing Strait of Hormuz supply fears that had briefly pushed oil above $100 last week.

items.detail: The FOMC decision lands **Wednesday, July 29 at 2:00 p.m. EDT**, and pricing has flipped to a hold: **CME FedWatch now shows a ~65% chance of no change** at the 3.50%–3.75% range, versus the ~35% hike odds carried into last week.
items.why: The collapse in oil back below $90 pulled the inflation impulse out of the market, shifting bets from a possible July hike toward a data-dependent pause, with the tightening debate pushed to September.

items.detail: The megacap earnings gauntlet begins after Monday's close this week: **Microsoft and Meta report July 29**, followed by **Apple and Amazon on July 30**, with Microsoft seen at ~$4.23 EPS on ~$87.6B revenue and Amazon guided to ~$196B in sales.
items.why: With the Fed on hold, investors will lean on Big Tech capex commentary and AI-cloud growth to judge whether the semiconductor scare is a genuine demand threat or a valuation reset.

items.detail: Indian equities snapped their five-session losing streak Monday: the **Nifty 50 jumped 228.50 points (0.96%) to 23,995.95** and the **Sensex surged 776.01 points (1.02%) to 76,835.78**, a decisive rebound from Friday's 23,767 close.
items.why: Sliding crude and easing West Asia tensions lifted sentiment and unwound the oil-import fear that had driven the prior week's slide.

items.detail: The relief is extending Tuesday, with the **Sensex and Nifty opening flat below 24,000** even as **Brent slid further to about $86.89 a barrel**, deepening a tailwind for India's import bill, trade deficit and rupee.
items.why: As a major net oil importer, India benefits mechanically from cheaper crude, but caution capped the open ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision and Tuesday's monthly F&O expiry.

items.detail: Global cues turned mixed overnight, with **Japan's Nikkei 225 down ~3.9%** and Korean and Chinese benchmarks in the red as the chipmaker rout spread across Asia, threatening to pressure Indian IT and tech-linked names.
items.why: The China lithography report that sank U.S. chip stocks Monday rippled into Asian semiconductor and hardware supply chains overnight.

items.detail: Foreign investors stayed on the sell side even into Monday's rally, with **FIIs offloading roughly ₹1,688 crore of cash equities** and holding a large net-short index-futures position, while **DIIs continued to absorb the supply**.
items.why: Elevated U.S. yields and a cautious pre-Fed stance kept foreign money trimming emerging-market exposure, leaving domestic institutions to underpin the bounce.

items.detail: **Bitcoin steadied near $64,850** (+0.3% Monday) after opening ~1.6% higher, clawing back from last week's break below $64K but stalling well short of reclaiming the $65K–$66K range.
items.why: Traders welcomed the Middle East de-escalation and falling energy prices as disinflationary, but held back from fresh buying ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.

items.detail: Ether outperformed again, **rising 1.6% to about $1,944** after opening 4.3% above Sunday, while **Solana added 0.7% to ~$75.84**, both recovering ground lost in Friday's risk-off slide.
items.why: The broader relief rally on cooling oil and geopolitical tension lifted higher-beta majors, with ETH continuing to draw the strongest bid.

items.detail: Sentiment remains fragile: the **Crypto Fear & Greed Index is still stuck in 'Fear' in the mid-20s to low-30s**, showing traders have not shaken the caution that built during last week's equity and ETF selloff.
items.why: A converging cluster of event risk — the Fed decision, the CLARITY Act deadline and market-structure uncertainty — is keeping positioning defensive despite the price stabilization.

items.detail: The regulatory clock is now the dominant swing factor: the **CLARITY Act faces an August 10 final deadline**, but a Senate floor vote before the recess remains uncertain after Republicans released updated bill text.
items.why: Passage would be the summer's biggest institutional catalyst by clarifying SEC/CFTC jurisdiction, while a stall or failure risks renewed downside pressure on Bitcoin.

crossCuttingTheme: Oil's collapse below $90 on U.S.–Iran de-escalation is the unifying driver — it has flipped Fed pricing from a possible hike to a ~65% hold, powered a near-1% rebound in Indian equities and steadied Bitcoin — but a new China lithography breakthrough has opened a second front, sending a fresh chipmaker rout from Wall Street across Asia and capping the risk-on relief.
